description: Change of use from Class C3 (dwellinghouse) to Class C4 (HMO for up to 5 persons), and the retention of a single storey rear extension (Part retrospective application).
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of the materially different and more intensive pattern of occupation associated with five unrelated adults living independently, would generate increased comings and goings, visitors, deliveries, frontage activity and use of the rear garden. In the context of this predominantly family-oriented and relatively quiet residential street, the development would cause unacceptable noise and disturbance to neighbouring occupiers. The submitted Noise Statement, HMO Management Plan and reliance on licensing and statutory nuisance controls would not adequately avoid or mitigate the ordinary operational impacts of the use. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy DP1 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The proposed development fails to provide sufficient on-site car parking for a five-person HMO in a PTAL 1b location and would displace additional parking demand onto streets already subject to high parking stress. The submitted parking survey contains material inconsistencies and, when its raw data are audited, demonstrates average parking stress of approximately 93% on Dickens Avenue and 88% across the wider survey area. Additional demand would increase the likelihood of obstructive and unsafe parking, vehicle conflict and harm to the safe and efficient operation of the highway. Furthermore, the proposed rear cycle store would not be safely and conveniently accessible because the access route is below the applicable 1.2 metre standard and is further obstructed by frontage parking. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMT 5 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T2, T4, T5, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies TR3, TR4 and TR6 of

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
